title: The Second Half Advantage
about:
A keynote-driven course from The Platform Nigeria, taught by Timilola Adetu, founder of SKLD Integrated Services Limited (formerly Schools Kit Limited), a sourcing company serving over 500 organisations across Nigeria.

At forty, after fourteen years in oil and gas, she left a secure corporate career with no business training to open a back-to-school store at Onikan. Over twenty-five years she grew it into a multi-division company, then handed it over and stepped into a third act. This course follows that second-half pivot: the mindset that made it possible, the discipline that carried it, the choice to let others scale it, and a succession that set her free. It is a practical study in transition for anyone who senses a bolder second half ahead.
benefits:
• Read the signals (job insecurity, flexibility, finances, health, purpose) that tell you change is coming
  • Tell a growth mindset from a fixed one, and respond to change without regret
  • Make a bold pivot the practical way: a proof of concept, a real bridge, eyes open
  • Bring corporate discipline to a young venture and lead from the shop floor
  • Let others into your vision so the business can outgrow you
  • Build range, find mentors, empower a team, and start before you feel ready

steps.title: The 18-month question, and that young lady is me

item.content:
Timilola opens with a question: could some part of your life look completely different in 18 months? Then she tells the story of a faultless corporate climber who walked away at forty, and reveals it is her own.

In this lesson

  • The question that unsettles even the most successful
  • The good girl who followed every rule, then left it all
  • Two careers: 14 years in corporate, then 25 in business

steps.title: Timilola at 40: what tipped the decision

item.content:
She walks through the mindset and the maths behind a very bold move: the spark of a business idea, the fear of downsizing, and a narrow window to act.

In this lesson

  • The spark: a back-to-school idea as her eldest son moved up
  • Job insecurity in an industry that rises and falls
  • Choosing a business that would always stay relevant

steps.title: Your reflections: the signals of change

item.content:
She turns the questions on you. What is your story? The honest reflections that signal it may be your turn to change.

In this lesson

  • The signals: security, flexibility, finances, health, family
  • Personal fulfilment, and the search for purpose
  • Why some of us are late bloomers, and that is fine

steps.title: Change is constant; mindset decides your response

item.content:
Change recurs all through her story. How you respond to it depends on the mind you bring. She defines mindset and makes the case for a growth one.

In this lesson

  • What a mindset actually is
  • A growth mind: your skills and abilities are not fixed
  • The courage to pivot at forty-plus

steps.title: Growth vs fixed mindset; respond without regret

item.content:
Two mindsets, two very different second halves. She contrasts the fixed mind with the growth mind, and urges an honest look at your own.

In this lesson

  • The fixed mind: if it ain't broke, don't fix it
  • Responding by acting quickly and positively, without regret
  • To thine own self be true: be honest about your mindset

steps.title: From VI to Onikan: the leap and the reality

item.content:
She trades an air-conditioned Victoria Island office for a shop at Onikan, opposite a mama put, and keeps her nerve when customers do not come.

In this lesson

  • Her husband's blessing: are you sure? I'll support you
  • The reality: area boys, a generator, no help desk
  • Holding her nerve through a seasonal lull

steps.title: Corporate discipline; roll up your sleeves

item.content:
The discipline of her corporate years stood her in good stead. She outsourced what she could not afford and led from the shop floor.

In this lesson

  • Outsource the services you cannot yet afford
  • No MD hat: serving customers and stacking shelves herself
  • Lay the example, or your staff will not follow

steps.title: The targets revelation: bringing in a COO

item.content:
Twelve years in, revenue had grown but so had the weight of running it alone. A consultant and a new COO changed everything with one idea: targets.

In this lesson

  • Arrived, but tired: the cost of running it all yourself
  • A COO who set revenue and performance targets
  • Revenue doubled within two years

assessment.title: Module 3 Check: Building It
assessment.description: A quick check on the leap, the discipline, and the targets revelation.

questions.question: Services she could not yet afford, like audit and accounting, she chose to ____.

item.content:
A growth mind accepts the ideas it did not think of. It was her vision, but she let others expand it and run with it, and the business grew.

In this lesson

  • Why a growth mind can accept other people's ideas
  • Letting others expand the vision and run with it
  • Diversifying into multiple business divisions

steps.title: Jobs and succession: 2 to 310, COO to CEO

item.content:
Growth you can count: from two staff to over three hundred, serving 500 organisations. And the COO she hired rose to lead the company she built.

In this lesson

  • Real jobs created across many states of Nigeria
  • Staff growth from 2 in 2000 to 310 last year
  • Succession: from COO to DMD to CEO

steps.title: It's not about age: brand, equity, never too late

item.content:
An ever more expansive mind launched a new brand and took on private equity. At sixty-five she walked a runway; at sixty-six she is still going strong.

In this lesson

  • Marcelle Hughes: her own uniform brand from a family name
  • Taking on private equity investment around sixty
  • It's not about age; the second half can be the boldest

steps.title: Don't be pigeonholed; change yourself, find mentors

item.content:
Build range, change what needs changing in you, and find people who have done it. She tells how she made herself assertive when told she never would be.

In this lesson

  • Don't be pigeonholed: move across roles and industries
  • Change yourself: the assertiveness she built on purpose
  • Find mentors, do the research, and know your onions

steps.title: Passion, pace, empower your team, and the third career

item.content:
Passion sustains you, so go at your own pace and empower your team for real. She closes with a charge, and a third career of writing and mentoring.

In this lesson

  • Passion is what sustains you; walk to your own clock
  • Empower your team for real, and don't take the power back
  • The charge: it's never too late to start
